chunks: Sa'd narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Sulayman, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Qasim ibn al-Hasan, from whomever narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He was asked about a man in the countryside who is unable to provide Fitrah, so he said: He should give charity of four Artals of milk.

key_terms.أَرْطَال: Artals, a unit of volume/weight measurement used in fiqh
key_terms.الْبَادِيَة: The countryside or rural area, implying a lack of access to standard markets or food supplies
key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Zakat al-Fitr, the obligatory alms-giving at the end of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What is the alternative Zakat al-Fitr for someone in the countryside who cannot provide grain or dates?
ai.summary: In al-Istibsar, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), highlighting the jurisprudential flexibility (takhfif) applied to rural dwellers lacking access to staple grains. By prescribing four Artals of milk, the Imam demonstrates the principle of substituting local, accessible commodities for the standard wheat or barley, ensuring the poor can still fulfill their religious duty through means available in their specific environment.
